case.title: Target written in UTC on 11 March is 00:30 on 12 March in Nairobi

submissions.open_text: Caretaker says the kiosk attendant opens late on weekends.
Boda rider's household treats pump water with chlorine tablets.
Night guard buys from a seller because his landlord disconnected the line.

case.why: Probes using the local calendar day. t is written as 2024-03-11T21:30:00+00:00, which is 2024-03-12T00:30 in Nairobi. n1 and n2 fall on local 2024-03-11. They are 0 m and about 44.5 m from t, so each would qualify on distance. Because they are on a different local day, t has zero same-day neighbours and same_spot must not fire. An implementation that would wrongly fire: one that groups by UTC date, or by the date prefix of the captured_at string, or that uses a rolling 24-hour window. Each of those puts t on 11 March, or within 24 hours of both neighbours, giving 2 neighbours. off_hours does fire on t, since 00:30 local is before 06:00. That is expected and listed. There is no burst: t is 9.5 hours after n2.
